analysis: Both changed files are test-only: CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift (head lines 10-12, 21, 456-491, 652-653, 674-675, 677-726) and the new CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift. The changes: (1) header comments say the suite now runs in the provider CI lane (scripts/run-provider-tests.sh) instead of being skipped; (2) new tests for a reconnect policy (close code 1012 reconnects within 0-1 s without backoff growth; sessions stable for the configured duration reset backoff); (3) helpers makeClient, reregistrationTime and withGrownReconnectBackoff, which pass a CoordinatorReconnectPolicy into CoordinatorClient. No production source is in this batch, so the actual CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorClient changes are not visible. Security-relevant points for integration: TB-002 coordinator-to-provider WebSocket availability. A coordinator-controlled close code 1012 skips backoff. The coordinator is trusted, so this is not an adversarial channel, but a fast reconnect storm on repeated 1012 would be a coordinator/availability concern. This is outside the test files and needs the production policy code to judge. Re-registration after a reconnect must still run the full attestation and authorization path (T-053, T-036). Tests only observe register messages, so they do not verify that a fast reconnect cannot bypass connection-bound App Attest authorization. The integration tests use a fake attestation signature against a loopback mock only, with no production secrets or trust-affecting code. Enabling the integration suite in CI introduces no new attack surface in the supplied evidence. No findings. I flag deeper review only to confirm the production reconnect policy in the other batch/files keeps jitter, bounded ranges and no unauthenticated fast-path.
